chunks: And that which was narrated - Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan from Najjah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

"When the Mu'tamir (one performing Umrah) enters Mecca, not being a Mutamatti', then he circles the House, and walks between Safa and Marwah, and prays the two rak'ahs behind the Maqam of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), let him return to his family if he wishes."
And he said, "Only the Umrah al-Mufradah and al-Mut'ah were revealed, because al-Mut'ah entered into Hajj, and Umrah al-Mufradah did not enter into Hajj."

So it is not contradictory to what we mentioned, because his saying (peace be upon him) 'and Umrah al-Mufradah did not enter into Hajj' means the Umrah that was performed in other than the months of Hajj, because Umrah al-Mufradah only enters into Hajj if it occurs in the months of Hajj. And whenever the matter is as we mentioned, it is not sufficient in place of al-Mut'ah. And as for that which indicates that if one performs al-Mut'ah, it has sufficed for Umrah al-Mufradah, added to what we mentioned, is that which was narrated:

key_terms.غَيْرَ مُتَمَتِّعٍ: Not being a Mutamatti' (one combining Umrah and Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Umrah al-Mufradah and Umrah al-Mut'ah in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi uses this narration from Imam al-Sadiq to clarify the jurisprudential distinction between Umrah al-Mufradah and Umrah al-Mut'ah, noting that the latter is subsumed within Hajj while the former remains independent unless performed during the Hajj months. This explanation resolves apparent contradictions in legal rulings by establishing that Umrah al-Mut'ah suffices for Umrah al-Mufradah, a principle rooted in the flexibility of Shia fiqh regarding ritual completeness.
